what_happened: The job to add version-pin and hermetic-check defaults and widen the reader budget was rejected. The final verdict was fail because the test check failed. The kept output shows the walltime tests passing (6 of 6). The failure line is "shard 3 of 6: 1 of 13 units failed: athena-cli --test drain". The output shows no test name or assertion for the drain failure. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet, and no blocker or major findings are listed. The failed check is a check that ran, not a criterion. The job is a config-class job and probably touched defaults and the reader budget, so a link to the drain test is plausible but not shown.
cause: The kept test output is the tail of a sharded CI run. It holds a passing walltime test binary and a one-line shard summary naming the failed unit (athena-cli --test drain). It holds none of the failing test's name, assertion or output. Nobody can tell from the record whether this job broke the drain test, whether the test was already broken or flaky, or whether it is config drift. Nothing keeps the failing unit's own output, and no baseline run of that unit on the unchanged base exists. The producer and verifier therefore cannot tell what failed, and the job is rejected on the test gate alone.
other_causes: Drain tests read the live athena.toml and defaults (earlier jobs 20261105-160208-p3hw and 20261104-194908-0hzr), so a defaults or config edit can break them without being named in the reading.
No baseline run of the failed unit on the unchanged base shows whether the job caused the failure.
open_hypotheses: The drain test failed because of this job's defaults or reader-budget change, for example a pinned value or budget figure.
The drain failure was pre-existing or flaky and unrelated to the job.
The drain test pins a live config or defaults value, which would fit the earlier config-pinning cases.
contradictions: The earlier cases of the same work type (config) mostly show criteria or findings from the verifier. This event lists no unmet criteria and no findings, only a failed check.
The kept output shows a passing test binary, not the failing one, so the visible evidence points away from the visible tests as the cause.
prevention: When a sharded test check fails, keep the failing unit's own output (test names, assertion messages) in the check record and not just the shard summary. Rerun the failed unit once on the unchanged base so the record says whether the job caused it. The producer and verifier would then see the cause, and a failure unrelated to the job would not be counted against it. The test gate's counts (44 ends, 0 disagreements) give no basis to relax or remove it.
proposed_request: When a test check fails in a sharded run, make Athena keep the full output of each failed unit (test names and assertion messages) in the check record, instead of the tail of the log. Also rerun each failed unit once on the unchanged base, and record whether it fails there too. Acceptance: (1) a failing unit in a sharded run produces a record containing its failing test names and assertion text; (2) the record states whether the same unit fails on the base; (3) a test shows both outcomes using a fixture that has one failing unit. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Then retry job 20261114-013056-pkhp (version-pin and hermetic-check defaults, widen reader budget) and report which drain test failed and why.
